prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1043; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this call?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please tell me where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened.

A: I was driving through Pearland, Texas, on a weekday afternoon. I was heading toward a shopping center and needed to make a left turn into the parking lot.

Q: Did you have a green light or were you turning on a yellow or a green arrow?

A: It was a green light, but there was no arrow. I was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic so I could turn.

Q: What happened next?

A: A vehicle coming from the opposite direction struck the front driver's side of my car as I was completing the turn. I didn't see it coming until right before impact.

Q: Did you brake or swerve before the impact?

A: I tried to brake, but there wasn't enough time to avoid it.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I didn't hit my head. My airbags did not deploy. But my body jerked forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Did you seek medical attention after the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They diagnosed me with a neck strain and a lower back strain.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially when I turn my head to check mirrors, and my lower back aches when I sit for long periods. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injuries?

A: I missed a few days and I've been working modified duties since then.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think I've covered it. I just want to get my car repaired and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
